holidays.name: Evaluate Your Life Day
holidays.description: A day set aside to step back, take stock of where you are, and decide whether your life is headed where you want it to go. Think of it as a performance review where you are both the boss and the employee.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance with murky origins, listed in quirky holiday calendars and popularized by online holiday compilations.
holidays.funFact: Many people use this day to write a pros-and-cons list of their life, which is basically a personal SWOT analysis without the corporate jargon.

holidays.name: National Seafood Bisque Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the silky, creamy, French-style soup made from shellfish like lobster, crab, or shrimp. Fans mark the day by slurping bowls of rich bisque, ideally with a dash of sherry and a lot of crusty bread.
holidays.origin: It is a food holiday found in national food-day calendars, celebrating a dish that comes from French culinary tradition.
holidays.funFact: Traditional bisque was thickened with ground shellfish shells and rice, so the crunchy bits that most people throw away were the secret to the soup's silky body.

holidays.name: I Love Lucy Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the classic sitcom and its fearless comedic star Lucille Ball, remembered for chocolate factory chaos, grape stomping, and Vitameatavegamin mishaps.
holidays.origin: The date marks the anniversary of the show's debut episode on CBS, which aired on October 15, 1951. Fans have since celebrated the series around mid-October, and some calendars place the observance on October 19.
holidays.funFact: I Love Lucy was one of the first sitcoms to be filmed in front of a live studio audience using multiple cameras, a technique that became the standard for TV comedy.

holidays.name: National Pumpkin Cheesecake Day
holidays.description: A day for indulging in the glorious fusion of fall's favorite gourd and the world's creamiest dessert. Whether graham cracker crust or gingersnap, spiced pumpkin cheesecake gets its moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food holiday that sprang up in the autumn dessert calendar, riding the wave of pumpkin-spice mania each October.
holidays.funFact: Pumpkin is technically a fruit, and so is cheesecake's other core ingredient base of cream cheese being... well, not a fruit, but the dessert still counts as a seasonal fruit dessert in the loosest and most delicious sense.

holidays.name: International Gin and Tonic Day
holidays.description: A bubbly salute to the iconic highball of gin, tonic water, and a wedge of lime. It is celebrated with a clink of glasses and a toast to the cocktail that started as medicine.
holidays.origin: The drink was born among British colonials in India, who mixed bitter quinine tonic, used to prevent malaria, with gin to make it more palatable. The day is an unofficial toast that cocktail lovers observe on October 19.
holidays.funFact: Tonic water glows bright blue under a black light because of the quinine it contains.
